claim: The small icons are a linear-light area average of the 96px mark, not a default resize

evidence_source: Owner asked 2026-09-06 whether the image quality could be improved. So 96 real pixels is the ceiling, and the quality loss was in the resampling rather than the source. An sRGB value is a perceptual encoding, not a quantity of light, so averaging those codes - the default in every image tool - averages the wrong thing and the white highlight on the olive comes out grey. Three methods were rendered at 16/32/48 and compared: sRGB Lanczos (current), linear-light Lanczos, and linear-light area average. Linear Lanczos was rejected outright - its negative lobes ring on edges this hard and put a black fringe around the olive at 48px that is nowhere in the source, with the darkest pixel landing at luminance 0. The area average cannot overshoot, and because 96 divides exactly by 16, 32 and 48 each output pixel is one whole n-by-n block, so it is not an approximation of the correct answer but the correct answer. Verified end to end: all three images inside the .ico match the generator's output exactly (max channel difference 0) and differ from a naive sRGB Lanczos by up to 47 levels. scripts/check-favicons.js recomputes the average and fails if any shipped icon is more than 1 level off; a default resize scores 38 and fails. NOTE: an earlier measurement in this session appeared to show linear-light performing worse at 32 and 48px - that metric used a box average as its reference and so was only measuring how much each filter rings, not which looked better.
